evals.prompt:
Can you do a rhythm audit on this piece? I want to know if the sentence structure is too flat.

---

The meeting started at nine. It was a long meeting. The team discussed the project. It was a complex project. Moreover, the timeline was tight. The manager spoke first. She outlined the key issues. The issues were numerous. Furthermore, the budget was limited. The team listened carefully. They took many notes. They asked several questions. The manager answered each one. She was thorough and precise. Consequently, the meeting ran long. It ended at noon. The team felt informed. They also felt tired. Additionally, they felt uncertain. The next steps were unclear.
evals.expected_output: A rhythm audit report that flags: very low sentence length CV (all sentences are 4-6 words), high transition word density (moreover, furthermore, consequently, additionally), repeated openers (It, She, They, The), and a run of same-length sentences. The overall assessment should clearly identify this as metronomic/flat prose.
expectations: The report runs the analysis script and reports numeric metrics
The report identifies low sentence length CV (below 35%)
The report flags high transition word density
The report flags repeated sentence openers
The overall assessment characterizes the prose as metronomic or flat
The report follows the prescribed format with all sections present

evals.prompt:
Check the rhythm of this essay — does it have good sentence variety?

---

The novel opens in the middle of an argument.

Not a dramatic one — no raised voices, no slammed doors — but the quiet, flattening kind that couples learn to conduct entirely through implication, through the slight edge in a question, the too-careful way one person picks up a glass. By page three we understand, without being told, that this marriage has been failing for years.

What Ferrante does in the first chapter that most novelists wouldn't dare is refuse to explain. She gives us the argument without context. We don't know who started it, or why, or what the stakes are. We are dropped in mid-sentence, mid-feeling, and expected to orient ourselves by paying attention.

This is actually the harder task for the reader — and the more rewarding one.

Most literary fiction announces its intentions early. Here is a family, here is its fracture, here is what the novel will ask of you. Ferrante withholds the frame. She trusts that confusion, properly handled, creates a kind of forward pressure, a need to read that no amount of beautiful prose can manufacture on its own.

The gamble pays off. By the time context arrives, we're already inside the marriage, already taking sides.
evals.expected_output: A rhythm audit report showing good sentence variety — high CV%, mix of very short and longer sentences, a stylistic fragment ('Not a dramatic one'), varied paragraph lengths. The overall assessment should be positive/good rhythm with only minor notes if any.
expectations: The report runs the analysis script and reports numeric metrics
The report identifies a healthy sentence length CV (above 45%)
The report detects the stylistic fragment ('Not a dramatic one')
The report identifies varied paragraph lengths
The overall assessment is positive — good rhythm, not flat
The report follows the prescribed format with all sections present
